Dear Julin,

It would be a good idea to combine the three environments together,
and concatenating the three sets would be one way to accomplishing
this. You can look at QTL main effects as well as the QTL-ebvironment
interactions.

One potential problem with the concatenating approach is an artificial
inflation of sample size. I wonder what Karl thinks about this, and
if there is a way around this in R/qtl right now.

The "right" way would be to fit a random effects model to incorporate
clutsering within lines.

Regards,
Saunak

> Date: Thurs 21 Dec 2006 11:23
> From: Julin Maloof
>
> Hello,
>
> I have a dataset where we have genotyped the same set of RILs in 3
> different environments. Part of our interests are in environment by
> QTL interactions. Currently I analyze each environment differently.
> Would it be valid in Rqtl to analyze them together, using the
> environment as a covariate? If I were to do this, should I give the
> RILs in different environments different names (even though they
> would be the same genotypes).
>
> Thanks for any advice,
>
> Julin
